description: Mullainathan and Shafir's experiments showed scarcity taxes the same person's cognitive performance, reducing effective intelligence and self-control by roughly a full standard deviation - making people appear less capable than they are.
source_name: Mani et al., Poverty impedes cognitive function, Science 341 (2013)

description: Scarcity produces intense focus on the pressing need at the expense of everything peripheral. Time-scarce people miss medical appointments; money-scarce people miss bill payments - not from indifference but because those things fall outside the tunnel.
energy_note: The dentist appointment was never a decision. It was invisible.

aspect: It is situational, and it lifts
description: Bandwidth is not permanently damaged. Farmers' cognitive capacity was restored as soon as crop payments arrived. When the pressure lifts, the capacity returns.
energy_note: The single most hopeful finding in this dataset.
notes: Important for the game: this is reversible, and saying so is accurate.

aspect: Immigration is a scarcity of the relevant kind
description: An open application with no decision date is scarcity of certainty. It occupies bandwidth continuously, for years, in exactly the way the research describes - and unlike money, no payment arrives to release it.

Social scarcity behaves the same way. In an Einstein Aging Study sample, higher daily loneliness predicted worse same-day processing speed and memory binding, and worse performance the next day - holding even after controlling for momentary depressed mood.
energy_note: The isolation is not just painful. It is measurably expensive.
notes: CALIBRATION: this literature is dominated by ageing and dementia-risk framing and causality runs both ways. The momentary within-person findings support the bandwidth reading; the longitudinal ones are weaker.

aspect: Which is the defensible version of the 'no ideas' claim
description: There is no evidence for a direct line from sexual or romantic dissatisfaction to fewer business ideas. There is good evidence that unresolved preoccupation of any kind - money, status, isolation, an open file - consumes the same bandwidth that side projects, risk-taking and original thinking run on.
energy_note: The ideas did not leave. The capacity to hold them did.
notes: Deliberately stated this way. The mechanism is real; the specific causal chain in the popular version is not established.

aspect: SCENARIO - the side project that never started
description: Omid had a design for a modular test rig in 2022. It is still four sketches and a spreadsheet. Every evening for three years has had a form in it, or a portal check, or a phone call about a form. He is not lazy and he has not lost interest. He has no slack.

The research names the antidote: slack, the buffer that allows decisions without constant trade-offs. Anything that creates certainty - a decision date, permanent status, a stable account - returns capacity directly.
energy_note: What actually helps, and it is not resilience.
